question: An engineer building an SDLC automation wants an agent to run git status, stage changes, and commit them as part of a scripted workflow, in addition to reading and editing source files. Which built-in Agent SDK tool grants this ability to run version-control commands directly?
options: A) Grep, which searches file contents with regex and has no ability to invoke external commands like git
B) Bash, which runs terminal commands and scripts, including git operations, in addition to other shell tasks
C) AskUserQuestion, which prompts the user with clarifying multiple-choice questions rather than executing shell commands
D) WebFetch, which retrieves and parses web page content and cannot execute local version-control commands
correct_answers: B) Bash, which runs terminal commands and scripts, including git operations, in addition to other shell tasks
explanations: Incorrect. Grep only searches file contents with regex; it cannot invoke git or any other external command.
Correct. Bash is documented as running terminal commands and scripts, explicitly including git operations, which covers status, staging, and committing.
Incorrect. AskUserQuestion is for gathering clarifying input from the user, not for executing version-control operations.
Incorrect. WebFetch retrieves remote web content; it has no capability to run local shell or git commands.
